## Screen projects for a GDPR data protection impact assessment

### How it works
A form describes one processing activity. A Set node holds the thresholds and the nine EDPB screening criteria live in a data table you can edit. A Code node scores the answers deterministically: each Yes answer and each keyword found in the description counts a criterion, and 10,000 people or more counts as large scale. A Groq call then reads the description and may add a criterion only when it quotes the exact words that show it; a suggestion without a verbatim quote is discarded. Two or more criteria mean REQUIRED, one means CONSIDER, none means NOT_REQUIRED, and an empty criteria table or a description too short to screen means INCOMPLETE, never a quiet pass. Every screening goes to dpia_screenings and every criterion met to dpia_findings with its evidence. REQUIRED is posted to Discord, and the form shows the verdict either way. Every Monday a schedule counts the week and posts a digest, including when nothing was screened.

### Setup
1. Add a Groq credential to the Groq node and a Discord webhook credential to both Discord nodes.
2. Run Set Up Tables once: it creates the three data tables and loads the nine criteria. Every other node finds its table by name.
3. Open the form and describe a project. Try one with health data and 50,000 people.
4. Tune Set Screening Policy and the keywords in dpia_criteria. Activate the workflow for the weekly digest.

### Customization tips
Keyword lists are English; add your own words per criterion. The judge is a model and can miss things, which is why it can only add, and only with a quote. This is a triage aid, not legal advice.

## 1. Create the tables and load the nine criteria (run once)
Three tables are created with typed columns, or reused if the names exist. The nine EDPB criteria are upserted by key, so running this twice changes nothing. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. Describe and score
The [form](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.formtrigger/) collects the project. Set Screening Policy holds the thresholds. Each Yes answer and each keyword hit counts one criterion; an empty criteria table or a short description gives INCOMPLETE.

## 3. Judge and decide
The [LLM Chain](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/) judge reads the description and may add a criterion only with a verbatim quote that is checked against the text. It can raise the verdict, never lower it.

## 4. Record
One row per screening in dpia_screenings with the verdict and the report, one row per criterion met in dpia_findings with its source and evidence, or a none row so every screening leaves a trace.

## 5. Escalate and answer
REQUIRED is posted through the [Discord](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.discord/) webhook, then the form shows the verdict page; every other verdict shows its own page with the reasons. Swap Discord for Slack or Gmail.

## 6. Weekly digest
The [Schedule Trigger](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger/) fires on Mondays once the workflow is active; run it by hand to test. Screenings inside lookback_days are counted per verdict and posted when anything needs attention, or when nothing was screened at all.
